newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Hasina asks police to strike hard at criminals.
newsitem.headline: Hasina asks police to strike hard at criminals.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, facing challenges from within and outside her party over her tough attitude to law and order, asked police on Saturday to deal harshly with "terrorism" and ensure public safety.

"Peace and order is a pre-requisite for development. And our police force must act impartially and boldly to free the country from terrorism," she said while opening the annual "police week" functions.
"The country needs political stability and social security to encourage development," Hasina said.

The official BSS news agency quoted her as saying that foreign and domestic investors had shown interest in Bangladesh but strict maintenance of law and order was imperative for economic rejuvenation.

The prime minister earlier asked police to arrest and punish criminals "without any consideration of their political identities". She also praised police for their uncompromising efforts to curb crime.
But recent police actions have turned a prominent legislator of Hasina's Awami League against her six-month-old government, and added fuel to opposition charges of police excesses.
The legislator, Abdul Kader Siddiqi, has demanded Home (Interior) Minister Rafiqul Islam should be sacked for "failure to run his ministry and perform his duties honestly".

His attack on the minister followed a police raid on his ancestral home in the northern district of Tangail, when his younger brother Azad Siddiqi was arrested for alleged acts of terrorism. Azad Siddiqi denies the charges.
Known as "Tiger Siddiqi" for his role as a guerrilla fighter in Bangladesh's 1971 war of independence against Pakistan, Kader Siddiqi regarded the arrest as a personal vendetta.
"The action was intended to defame me and my family," he said.
The dispute flared up as the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), headed by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, criticised "mass arrest and persecution of BNP activists".
BNP sources said on Saturday they would use Siddiqi's allegation to back up their charges of police excesses on opposition activists.
"The battle within Hasina's party shows how fragile her administration is...and we are going to focus on it," it said.
Siddiqi, however, said he had no dispute with Hasina but insisted she must sack her "inefficient" home minister.
